expectations.text: Includes a dedicated, sourced section addressing title status / titled land vs Rights of Possession risk specific to Boquete
expectations.evidence: output.md has a dedicated section "Before you shortlist anything here" (titled 'Title status: mixed — verify per lot.') explaining that developed town-area land is generally titled while outlying coffee finca land toward Jaramillo/Volcancito is commonly derecho posesorio (rights of possession), including mechanics (can't be conventionally mortgaged, months to convert, foreigners typically hold via a Panamanian corporation) and an actionable instruction to check the finca number at the Public Registry. It is sourced: the Sources list cites 'Title vs. ROP: Understanding Property Rights in Panama — Casa Solution' and 'Rights of Possession Panama, Derecho Posesorio — Best Places in the World to Retire', both with a Boquete-specific note. The structured AreaEditorial record also sets titleStatus: 'mixed' with a matching titleNote field, and the transcript documents the codebase's explicit warning that this field 'is not to be set from general knowledge' — the run treated that as the organizing constraint.

expectations.text: Includes at least one concrete cost-of-living or cost-to-buy figure with a named source
expectations.evidence: The specs table and pricing section give concrete cost-to-buy figures: 'Entry price $121,223 (Boquete Country Club, resale)', 'Published inventory from $214,600 (Towncenter Boquete)', 'Upper range $625,000', and Pino Alto Boquete '$245,000–$395,000' — all traced in the Sources list to 'v2/data/airtable.json — this site's own published project data for Boquete'. Neighborhood- and market-level figures (e.g. 'typical three-bedroom house in the Alto Boquete area runs $280,000–$380,000') are attributed collectively to named outlets in the Sources list (Global Property Guide, TheLatinvestor, Esales Overseas Property), explicitly flagged as 'broker-reported rather than authoritative' rather than hidden.

expectations.text: Includes an explicit 'who this suits / who it doesn't' section naming a type of buyer it is NOT good for
expectations.evidence: Section header "### Who Boquete suits — and who it doesn't" explicitly names the good-fit buyer (retirees/remote workers wanting cooler weather and an expat community) and then names buyer types it does NOT suit: people who 'need serious medical infrastructure close by,' anyone wanting nightlife/big-box shopping/variety, and implicitly flippers ('Boquete buyers are overwhelmingly people relocating for lifestyle, not flippers, and the market rewards patience over speed').

expectations.text: Includes practical access information (distance/time to nearest airport, road quality, whether a car is required)
expectations.evidence: A dedicated "### Getting there" section states the nearest airport (Enrique Malek International, David, IATA: DAV), drive time (40–50 minutes), flight option from Panama City (Copa/Air Panama), and full driving time from Panama City (6–7 hours via Pan-American Highway). Road quality is addressed in the who-it-suits section: 'unpaved roads on the outskirts can get genuinely difficult, and landslides on the steeper hillside routes aren't unheard of after a hard week of rain.' Whether a car is required is not stated as a single explicit sentence, but it is strongly and consistently implied throughout (every neighborhood is described by drive time/distance from town, no public transit or taxi infrastructure is mentioned, and 'most buyers fly into David... rather than driving'). Two of the three named sub-components are explicit and the third is a reasonable inference from the surrounding text, so the overall expectation is met.
output.md has 8 FAQ entries under '### FAQ': titled vs ROP, can foreigners buy, weather, distance from Panama City, cost to buy, which neighborhood for expats, healthcare access, and safety.

expectations.text: The page does not spend more than a sentence or two on scenery/atmosphere description disconnected from a purchase question (avoids travel-writing drift)
expectations.evidence: The 'Boquete in brief' section stays largely functional (location, population, climate rationale for buyers) with one clause of pure scenery: 'a dormant volcano you can hike overnight for a sunrise view of both the Pacific and Caribbean on a clear day.' The coffee paragraph ties back to real estate ('surrounding fincas are part of what gives the area its identity — and its zoning patchwork of small agricultural holdings mixed in with newer residential development'). No section is devoted to restaurants, tourism activities, or extended scene-setting; atmosphere language is kept to roughly one sentence and is otherwise in service of a buying-relevant point (climate, title risk, neighborhood choice).

claims.claim: Boquete town/district elevation is ~1,200 m (~3,900 ft)
claims.evidence: Transcript states this was cross-checked against Wikipedia after finding a conflicting lower-quality figure (256 m) elsewhere, and Wikipedia's ~1,200 m figure is consistent with independently known geography for Boquete's town center.

claims.claim: Every specific number in the output traces to a cited source (transcript, section 4)
claims.evidence: Mostly true, but not fully: the claim 'more than 3,000 permanent foreign residents from over 30 countries, by most recent counts' in the 'Boquete in brief' section has no specific citation tying it to any single item in the Sources list — it reads as a web-search-derived figure folded in without individual attribution, unlike the more carefully hedged pricing and appreciation figures elsewhere in the piece.

claims.claim: titleStatus was set to 'mixed' rather than left 'unknown' or asserted as 'titled', per the codebase's sourcing requirement
claims.evidence: Transcript section 2 quotes the actual code comment ('Do not set these from general knowledge — each one needs a real source') and section 4 explains the specific reasoning (outside restricted zones + finca land commonly ROP) with named sources, matching what appears in the delivered AreaEditorial record and titleNote.

claims.claim: No repo files were modified; the deliverable is a content draft only, not a code change
claims.evidence: Transcript section 5 states this explicitly, and the session's git status (reported as clean at conversation start) is consistent with no working-tree changes from this run.

claims.claim: The population figure (~19,000) is presented as current in the reader-facing copy
claims.evidence: The visible page copy states 'Boquete is a district and town of roughly 19,000 people' with no caveat that this is a 2008 census figure. The staleness is disclosed only in the transcript's internal notes and not in the FAQ or body text a site visitor or editor would see, so a reader has no way to know the number may be outdated.

suggestions.assertion: Includes practical access information (distance/time to nearest airport, road quality, whether a car is required)
suggestions.reason: This run passes on the strength of explicit airport distance/time and road-quality content, but never states outright that a car is required to get around Boquete day-to-day — that part is only inferable from context (every neighborhood described by drive time, no transit mentioned). An output that omitted car-necessity entirely but nailed the other two sub-points would pass this assertion identically. Consider splitting into two assertions or requiring an explicit statement about car dependency, since 'do I need a car to live here' is a distinct, common buyer question from 'how do I get to the airport.'

suggestions.assertion: Includes at least one concrete cost-of-living or cost-to-buy figure with a named source
suggestions.reason: The output mixes figures with strong per-source attribution (project prices tied to airtable.json, neighborhood elevations tied to Casa Solution) with figures attributed only to a vague collective ('brokers report... roughly 6% a year', '$4,200/m² from brokers'). The assertion as worded would also pass on the vague-attribution figures alone, since it only requires 'a named source' to exist somewhere on the page rather than requiring the specific number in question to carry a direct, checkable citation.

No assertion checks whether the population/demographic figures presented as current are actually current, or at least flagged as dated in the reader-facing text. This run cites a 2008 census population figure (~19,000) and an unsourced-in-line foreign-resident count (3,000+ from 30+ countries) as plain facts in the visible copy, with the staleness caveat living only in the transcript's internal reasoning — a reader of the published page would have no way to know. This is a real quality gap on a page whose whole premise is sourcing discipline, and it went uncaught by all six expectations.

eval_feedback.overall: All six expectations pass, and on inspection the underlying output genuinely earns each one — this is a substantively researched, well-sourced draft, not a superficial pass. The two access-information and cost-figure suggestions above are minor discriminating-power notes rather than signs of a bad grade. The more notable finding is the third suggestion: dated/unattributed demographic figures presented as current fact in reader-facing copy, which no current assertion is positioned to catch.
